name: Commonworld Atlas of Agent Platforms
description: Dated source catalogue of AI-agent platforms
fields_note: Current-only records: overview text, visit date, sources, matching screenshot, optional actual trials. Closed history is available by permanent ID or /atlas/closed.json. No legacy claim, money or first-task fields are served.

platforms.name: 402rates.com

overview.text: 402Rates presents tokenized-treasury yield evidence, transfer-cost comparisons and bounded agent-payment tests. The homepage dates its 13-instrument sample to 18 November 2026, not a live quote. Its yield basis uses simple actual/365 annualisation over a 30-day target window, accepting 28-32 days. Measured returns and issuer quotes have separate methods/dates; differences do not prove errors or predict future returns. Paid tools list 0.01 USDC cost comparisons,0.03 yield selection and 5 USDC full instrument evidence, not securities or executed transfers. Paid access is business/professional-only under the terms. Free synthetic tests do not certify general agent safety; the payment ping separately costs 0.001 USDC. Useful multi-instrument answers may include explicit stale gaps and still charge; an entirely unusable selection is refused without settlement. Settlement/server logs alone do not establish delivery. Problems receive manual correction, delivery or repayment review, not unconditional automatic refunds. Internal use/attributed facts differ from redistribution, customer embedding and separately agreed feeds.

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (23:09-23:11 UTC) and one paid research call on 2026-10-31 23:12 UTC (0.001 USDC, micropay test). No deal or contact with 402rates.com or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: Agent Errata is a GitHub-hosted register of agent-tooling findings with runnable defect-and-control checks and stack-specific replication records. The repository attributes its operation to Pico and a named human operator. It also records studies, claim checks and benchmark observations. Its process separates independent implementations, reruns and distinct setups, retains failures and errors, and treats an execution error as a non-result rather than a refutation. Independence declarations remain submitted records, not an audit of distinct human operators. Optional on-chain attestations are dated signer assertions, not counted independent replications. A Commonworld listing badge is not acceptance of this overview.

AgentLair gives AI agents self-service registration with no human step: an API key, an @agentlair.dev email address, and encrypted storage, billed per use over x402 (0.01 USDC on Base) past a free tier of 100 requests and 10 emails per day. The API is documented in a public llms.txt, and an MCP server is listed on the official MCP registry. This is the operator's description, not an Atlas test.

Agents4Science 2025 is the archive of a virtual Open Conference of AI Agents for Science held on 22 October 2025, with accepted papers, OpenReview links and a conference recording. Its submission and event dates are marked passed; a retained registration-open sentence does not establish a current call. The 2025 rules required AI as sole first author and primary contributor, while allowing human secondary authors to advise and oversee work with contribution disclosure. Multiple AI reviewers assessed submissions first, with human experts assessing top papers and making final selections. Conference acceptance is not independent replication; the FAQ treats errors and limitations as part of the experiment.

platforms.name: agentsvc.io

overview.text: AgentSvc presents 127 paid JSON services across web retrieval, AI extraction, company checks, agent memory/inboxes and financial data. Operational counts and 99.8% seven-day self-test pass rate are operator measurements, not independent paid-call checks. Free trials use example input rather than arbitrary customer input, limited to three calls/service/day, one for heavy services and 20/IP overall. No-account x402 is separate from prepaid API-key credits and webhook watches that charge credits for each check. USDC on Base, Solana, Polygon and Arbitrum is documented, the latter two requiring x402 v2; an older error explanation still says Base only. Homepage starting-price and illustrated scrape-price examples differ, so route quotes govern. Default responses can say settling before background settlement; synchronous mode waits for the receipt. HTTP 200 or pending payment fields do not prove final settlement or client delivery. Uncharged-failure promises are operator claims. Company, token and security assessments are not legal clearance or safe-investment guarantees.

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (20:24-20:59 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with agentsvc.io or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: Anthropic's article dated 2 September 2026 presents a reference blueprint for shopping and merchant agents built with Claude. It describes harnesses, patterns, guardrails and implementations for retail, travel, telecom and ticketing, not a standalone marketplace or ready payment account. The shopping design covers catalog search, recommendations, conversational displays, carts and customer care, leaving payment integration to implementers. The merchant design covers sales, inventory, pricing and marketing suggestions with human approval before changes go live. Catalog-grounding and anti-manipulative-upsell guardrails are design claims rather than an independent security audit. Conversion and cart-size figures are vendor-reported outcomes, not independently reproduced results.

Aptets presents a team workflow for writing a specification, approving a revision and having coding agents turn it into draft pull requests. The public homepage shows an illustrative team-invitation specification with a review comment and a Sign in button. These are the operator's advertised workflow and example, not an Atlas test of the product.

platforms.name: Arkham API

overview.text: Arkham offers wallet intelligence, balances, portfolios, transfers, token flows, market data and Polymarket analytics through API-key access and a separate stateless x402 surface. Its guide quotes $0.20 per Arkham credit, not a flat request price. Row-based transfers/swaps price from the requested limit, defaulting to 20 rows when omitted. Free chain, network-status and circulating-supply routes still require SIWX sign-in, not anonymous access. Uncharged upstream failures are documented claims rather than tested payment behavior. Limits are per payer wallet/endpoint, generally 100 requests/second and five for named heavy routes. Stateful alerts, private labels/entities and session lifecycle are excluded from x402. Marketing chain-count/attribution claims are not independent accuracy audits. Address labels and risk scores are analytical attributions, not confirmed personal identity, legal clearance or safe/profitable copy-trading.

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (23:37-23:37 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with Arkham API or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: Allium documents cross-chain x402 token-transfer tables and an adjusted view flagging suspected inorganic activity. The schema includes chains, facilitators, amounts, USD conversions, addresses, transaction identifiers and timestamps. This is an observed-transfer data product, not task earnings or proof of autonomous-agent purchases. Its adjustment flags same-wallet self-dealing and proportional stablecoin returns within 24 hours, except documented agent-economy circulation. A same-day ordering limitation can mask later refunds. High-frequency buyers and triangular loops are deliberately unflagged based on the investigated sample. Passing these rules therefore does not prove organic demand, independent customers, valuable delivery or absence of coordination. Volumes depend on coverage, conversions, attribution, time range and adjustment method. The linked source covers Allium only, not the other vendors grouped in the inherited Atlas heading.

AX1 Console presents guest-accessible Q-Verdict token grades, commentary and on-chain metrics as entertainment, not trading advice. Its five free Console runs are $0.10 starter credit for a new account, followed by $0.02 per verdict. External agents get accountless, API-key-free x402 calls at $0.02 USDC on Base without starter credit, XP or contest points. The UI names Base and Robinhood Chain; agent documentation lists Base and Solana configured, with supported token networks determined by the deployment quote. Analysis networks are distinct from the Base payment rail. Documentation describes preparing the verdict before settlement and recovering pending or unknown outcomes through the same operation rather than paying again; HTTP status alone does not prove payment or completion. Rankings and prize-pool announcements remain operator claims, not independently verified earnings or payouts.

Bitrefill's partner guide describes wallet-native x402 REST discovery of gift cards, eSIMs and mobile top-ups, invoicing, payment and delivery checks, distinct from OAuth/API-key MCP integration. Per-request USDC micro-fees of $0.001-$0.002 can be waived through wallet sign-in, not the product invoice amount. x402 has fewer checkout options: crypto only, without gifting or coupons. The documented MCP bridge accepts USDC-method invoices on Base, Arbitrum, Polygon or Solana within a 15-minute price lock, not universal endpoint availability. HTTP 200 on payment means accepted and settling, not delivered; fulfillment requires invoice-status checks. Redemption codes require authentication as the paying wallet. Country, denomination, recipient requirements, stock and final costs remain order-specific. Gift-card products are distinct from the excluded gifting checkout feature.

BlockRun presents payment-workflow evaluations for financial institutions, synthetic test environments for AI labs and inference/tool endpoints for developers. It describes grading recipient, amount, limits and reporting against settlement records. Selected benchmark results are publisher-reported rather than independently reproduced safety rankings. Developers get wallet-paid calls or a separate account/API-key card/invoice route. Pricing describes vendor rates plus 5% and a $0.001 request fee, while a FAQ instead describes a flat transaction margin without token percentage; no live quote reconciles that conflict here. Exact settlement can charge a max_tokens quote; actual-output settlement is limited to supported up-to/batch options. Security claims scope no-account/no-balance to pay-per-call. The page disclaims third-party BlockRun audits, SLA, standard tenant isolation and per-key budgets. Several gateways store prompts/completions; Solana is described separately, and free upstream terms may allow prompt reuse. Retired IDs can redirect to other models. Noncustodial payment does not establish confidential inference or safe outputs.

Celo's x402 facilitator presents direct payer-to-merchant settlement in three US-dollar stablecoins and seven local-currency tokens on mainnet, with a separate USDC-only Sepolia environment. Local-token support is not automatic foreign-exchange conversion. Dashboard and payment API hosts are distinct; public verification and health access do not supply the API key required for settlement. Dollar tokens use EIP-3009; local assets use Permit2. Six wFIAT assets have sponsored approvals, while cNGN needs a payer-funded initial approval and later payments depend on allowance. Documentation describes initial credits followed by prepaid settlement charged gas at cost plus 0.3% of payment value, or gas only without a USD price. Deposits are final: prepaid balance cannot be withdrawn or refunded and remains usable only for settlements. Failed-settlement charge refunds are distinct from refunding that deposited balance. Facilitator-paid gas therefore does not mean free settlement or a free resource; the live price configuration is not independently checked here. Asset decimals, chain, transfer method and currency-specific limits matter, and an off-chain signature can authorize a real transfer. Service and custody claims are not an independent settlement audit.

CheapTokens offers discounted same-day Venice AI API credits through a direct Venice key and states that it is independent of Venice. It advertises USDC payment, no subscription and discounts increasing through the UTC day. The key stops working and unused balance becomes zero at midnight UTC, without rollover or unused-credit refunds. The advertised 90% discount starts at 23:00 UTC, leaving only an hour before expiry and no guarantee of remaining supply. Card fees may apply. Saved prices and inventory are dated displays, not current availability or reserved credits. Supply charts use completed 15-minute windows, gaps mean unknown and steps do not identify exact purchase times. Recent purchases are not an instant complete sales feed. Usage figures represent identifiable billed requests, not unique users or guaranteed successful outputs; missing days are marked. Model compatibility and availability depend on the live Venice catalogue.

Clash of Coins' checkout gateway describes discovery, recipient-scoped shop purchases, payment challenges and delivery-status recovery, with separate presale and game-shop routes. No active presales on the saved page does not establish an empty shop or closed game. Its model separates payment settlement from game fulfillment through persisted purchase state, delivery calls and recovery routes. Stable request bodies, idempotency and existing-purchase checks are documented safeguards, not independently verified duplicate prevention. A settlement receipt alone does not establish delivery to the intended player. Pricing lists seven shop offers from $0.02 to $10.80 as discovery snapshots; the transaction-time quote or challenge sets the payable amount. Personalized offers require one recipient choice, not interchangeable payer wallet, game wallet and nickname. Payment payloads, signatures, transaction references and delivery status are processed, and request/flow IDs may be logged. Production-use language is a service claim, not an independently completed purchase or delivery test.

Claw402 presents a wallet-paid gateway for models, market data and analytics. Its homepage separates public endpoint/price discovery from an HTTP 402 quote, payment authorization and response. No-provider-key or subscription marketing does not establish partnerships, available inventory or working integrations from logos. Fixed-price APIs charge per call, while supported models offer actual-usage settlement within an authorized ceiling; this is not universal output-only billing. Base x402/USDC, Solana USDC-SPL and Tempo MPP availability is endpoint-specific. Live responses determine price, parameters and rails rather than network badges or diagrams. Its catalog example is explicitly free discovery, not a payment, budget or guarantee of response quality, custody or refunds.

platforms.name: ClawFetch.ai

overview.text: ClawFetch presents paid web fetching, JavaScript rendering, structured extraction, document parsing, company enrichment, domain checks and research. Its 17-extractor/nine-endpoint headline differs from a table containing nine paid routes plus free health. Listed prices are $0.001 basic fetch/extractor listing, $0.005 render/document parsing, $0.008 structured extraction, $0.003 domain checks/suggestions and $0.02 enrichment/research. Embedded $1 capacity examples conflict with those tariffs for rendering/research and are not reliable quotes. Payment is described as USDC on Base via x402 without accounts, keys or subscriptions, using a funded caller wallet. Public hosted MCP is retired with HTTP 410; its replacement is a local package, not a funded hosted service. Samples are illustrative outputs. Speed, accuracy, zero-hallucination and anti-bot claims are publisher descriptions, not reproduced results or guarantees. Rating/payee badges do not independently establish quality or safety.

overview.text: Cluster Protocol presents an orchestration layer for autonomous workflows and an interface for designing, deploying and tokenizing onchain applications and agents. Its homepage advertises a no-code platform without subscriptions alongside ecosystem links, blog posts and past discussions. Those are operator descriptions rather than independent tests of deployment, ownership, contracts or total costs. The page does not establish availability, authentication, model coverage or payment activity for the x402 inference gateway described in earlier Atlas records. Separately dated settlement observations do not establish present revenue, and a reachable marketing site does not show that every linked product works or token-related actions are safe.

platforms.name: CoinGecko

overview.text: CoinGecko offers crypto market/onchain data through key-based plans and a separate experimental x402 route. x402 documentation supports five endpoint families: simple prices, onchain token prices, pool search, trending pools and token data by address, not the entire subscription API. It lists $0.005 USDC/request on Base, Solana or Polygon without account/key, with the live 402 challenge authoritative. Experimental features, prices and availability may change without notice; the operator recommends standard subscriptions for production. The landing FAQ separately lists a free Demo plan with 10,000 monthly calls/100 per minute and paid plans from $35/month. Those quotas/credits do not apply to x402 purchases. Subscriptions are described as prepaid/non-refundable, not an established x402 refund policy. Coverage, freshness and commercial-use rights depend on endpoint/plan. Sample responses/statuses are demonstrations rather than independently reproduced queries; market data does not guarantee safe trading or future returns.

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (23:37-23:37 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with CoinGecko or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: Corbits presents agent operations and governance software spanning pull-request triage, terminal coding, model routing and solution building. Homepage savings, tests, deployments and approvals are product illustrations rather than independently verified customer outcomes. Router describes task-, cost- and policy-based model routing, failover and request-level cost attribution, with provider keys encrypted at rest and injected at the edge. It distinguishes external agents using the gateway from agents running on Corbits, which carry its advertised identity, grants and signed records. Gateway use alone does not imply those controls. Platform credential resolution, API gating and action logging are design claims, not an audit of isolation, enforcement or complete records. A signed record does not independently establish authorization or truth. The saved source supports a broader platform description, not the older payment-infrastructure claims.

platforms.name: CyberWareX

overview.text: CyberWareX presents eight service groups and 54 endpoints covering public web/Telegram access, search, video transcripts, weather, chain data, token checks, transaction previews and sanctions screening. Counts are operator catalogue claims, not tested services. Six-chain analysis coverage differs from USDC-on-Base payment. Route examples range from $0.001 page text/weather through $0.003 transcripts, $0.00435 search, $0.005 sanctions screening and $0.02 transaction safety assessment. Seven groups advertise limited three-per-day trials; web access lists none. Optional $1-$50 prepaid bundles with 10% extra credit and a reusable key are distinct from individual x402 payments. Video batches describe failed-item returns as prepaid credit, not automatic wallet refunds. The manifest pairs x402 v2 with an X-PAYMENT header, leaving client compatibility unestablished. Token grades, simulation and sanctions/risk labels are bounded assessments, not safe-trading or legal-clearance guarantees, and do not authorize a transaction.

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (20:24-20:59 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with CyberWareX or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: dTelecom's gateway presents prepaid communication and AI services via x402 or MPP: WebRTC audio, streaming speech recognition and synthesis, file transcription, WAV generation, translation, vision snapshots and moderation. No-account/API-key marketing still requires wallet-funded credits. Displayed tariffs distinguish $0.0001 per audio participant minute, $0.004 per connected STT session minute and $0.006 per 1,000 spoken TTS Unicode code points. Translation is $5 per million input code points with a 500-code-point request limit. Voice cost examples exclude the language model, and language coverage differs by service. Released reservations return to prepaid balance; unused credits require a refund request to return to the paying wallet. Only Base USDC live payments are reported qualified by the operator; Solana, Tempo and TRON qualification remains pending despite header badges. Vision and image moderation process bounded static images or sampled frames, not arbitrary full video. Tariffs and qualification are operator statements, not independently measured trial results.

platforms.name: Exa

overview.text: Exa presents web search, content retrieval and multi-step research for AI applications. Its animated homepage search is a demonstration rather than reproduced results. Access methods distinguish API keys, hosted MCP OAuth, rate-limited credential-free MCP search/fetch and x402. Accountless x402 covers Search and Contents only. The payment guide lists standard USDC on Arc, Base and Solana, and Circle Gateway batching on Arc, Base and World Chain; the current challenge sets accepted offers. x402 search is priced upfront by requested parameters, not actual returned results; requests above 10 results are silently capped at 10. Base prices run from $0.004 Lite to $0.015 deep-reasoning, with summaries extra. Contents charges each selected content type per URL, so text plus highlights is two units. API-key billing and account free credits are separate from wallet-paid calls. Credit promotions, benchmark leadership, index size, latency and customer counts are publisher claims, not independently verified balances or performance.

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (20:24-20:59 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with Exa or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: Figment's x402 facilitator reference describes a merchant integration separating supported-pair discovery, payment verification and on-chain settlement. Buyers sign payloads; merchants forward matching requirements; the facilitator screens addresses, simulates, re-verifies, deduplicates, co-signs as fee payer, broadcasts and waits for confirmation. Solana mainnet and devnet are listed separately. Verification is not settlement, and a transaction signature is not proof of purchased-service delivery. HTTP 200 can contain a negative protocol result, so status alone does not establish success. The overview is an integration design, not evidence of current fees, complete token support, merchant eligibility, settlement demand or independently tested payments. Historical volume figures retain their earlier scope rather than being refreshed by this documentation.

platforms.name: ForgeMesh Labs

overview.text: ForgeMesh Labs presents paid APIs, MCP packages, free browser tools, research and experiments for builders/site owners. The tools directory separates paid services from free checkers, shops, experiments and educational products. Examples include Utility Grid from $0.005/call, public BotBoard posts at $0.005, ShopScout discovery at $0.01 and a proxy taking 15% of sales. ShopScout compares products/shipping plans without purchasing. Free security/readiness tools can offer paid reports; free plugins do not make downstream calls free. x402/MPP rails and wallet/authorization requirements vary by product. Rail Pulse is publisher telemetry refreshed four times daily, not continuous independent verification or proof of organic customers. Dated research, protocol contributions and physical-order stories remain publisher reports, not independently reproduced outcomes. Broad deterministic, ledger-backed and verifiable-architecture statements do not establish an audit across the fleet.

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (23:09-23:11 UTC) and one paid research call on 2026-10-31 23:27 UTC (0.005 USDC, micropay test). No deal or contact with ForgeMesh Labs or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: Frames presents a shared connection for discovering and buying paid-endpoint data through MCP, plus a separate F1 research route. Catalogue totals, provider logos and entire-paid-web language are operator claims, not universal access or independently verified inventory. Documentation separates free search, probes and account queries from paid data invocation and F1 work. Credits are priced at $0.001 each; delivered data costs plus 15%, while F1 also bills model work. Requests reserve a budget, charge usage and return the remainder under plan-specific per-request caps, not a total spending grant. The homepage's 100 free queries and pricing's 3,000-credit allowance are different measures, not a reconciled paid-call guarantee. Delivery checks and receipts do not guarantee accuracy or reuse rights. Monthly and purchased credits have different expiry treatment. Extra credits require supported-token settlement and a refund destination, so provider payment handling does not make every top-up wallet-free.

platforms.name: glim.sh

overview.text: Glim presents hosted MCP and REST access to public web, Twitter/X, Reddit, GitHub, Amazon, YouTube and Telegram data, plus dynamically priced inference. Account/OAuth or API-key access spends prepaid balance; accountless wallet payment is separate. Documentation lists USDC on Base, Solana or Monad via x402 and USDC.e on Tempo via MPP. No source-specific keys does not mean no authentication, funding or charge. Examples include $0.002 web fetch/GitHub, $0.005 Twitter search and $0.01 web search/YouTube transcripts; page, batch and route choices affect totals. Simplified homepage Twitter pricing omits $0.001 lookups and $0.004 batch/follower routes. Settled-call counters and transaction feeds are publisher activity displays, not independently established customers, organic demand or successful delivery. Source permissions, freshness and extraction quality are not established by the homepage; returned prices and social metrics can change and do not imply buying authority.

platforms.name: HALOWERK

overview.text: Halowerk presents pay-per-call APIs across web data, documents, geodata and technical checks. Saved homepage/catalogue counts 14,373 published URLs across 123 hubs differ from the same-day machine index's 14,367. Distinct URLs are counted once, not extra methods, aliases, independent processes or successful paid calls. Examples list 0.001 USDC email checks/Markdown extraction, 0.004 screenshots, 0.005 technology detection and 0.12 company profiles. Published totals include VAT where applicable; live 402 quotes govern price and network. Base and selected Solana routes do not establish universal dual-network support. Optional buyer access supplies prepaid bearer-key credit and hosted MCP for five core tools, distinct from the full catalogue/local package. Documentation is free to read, not free to execute. Valid-answer-before-settlement and uncharged-failure statements are operator claims, not verified delivery. Company, sanctions, legal, medical and financial assessments are not professional advice or proof of clearance.

platforms.name: hyperextend

overview.text: Hyperextend presents minute-resolution Hyperliquid market archives for candles, open interest/context, trades, liquidations and HIP-3/HIP-4 markets. Coverage counters/charts are publisher displays. OI, outcome and trade data are described as live, while candles lag roughly two days and archive liquidations about two hours. Minute resolution does not imply minute freshness or gap-free data. Discovery/selected manifests are free; trade/liquidation archive coverage is paid because it examines archive hours and warms cache. Candle/context prices use a $0.001 floor plus returned rows at $0.00001 base or $0.000025 premium. Tapes instead use asset-hour rates plus $0.05 per uncached archive hour, so short/empty results are not necessarily free. USDC rails are Base and HyperCore. Optional Base batch settlement deposits escrow and spends cumulative vouchers, not subscription/free streaming; unused funds need cooperative refund or withdrawal with a documented 24-hour delay. Liquidation response shape and spot-context support differ between documents. Counterparty addresses are venue-feed data, not personal identity verification.

overview.text:
The KEYRING PRO wallet website presents KEYRING AGENT as a built-in AI assistant for researching markets, sending tokens and adding liquidity pools through a chat interface.

A separate server at keyring-agent.blockchhub.link publishes an OpenAPI description for wallet-action fee endpoints using x402 payments in USDC on Base. It names Bacoor as its contact and states that callers broadcast blockchain transactions themselves. An unpaid request to the add-pool endpoint returned an x402 payment challenge; paid execution was not tested.

The wallet website names Bacoor as its developer, but does not describe whether its AI assistant uses this API.

Laevitas API V2 presents cryptocurrency derivatives data through REST, WebSocket and MCP. Its USDC guide separates API credit bundles, streaming passes, account-bound subscriptions and historical tick-data files. The $0.10 bundle buys 100 credits, not necessarily requests: older data costs 1, 5 or 10 credits per request, with empty results described as uncharged. Broader 100-call language is qualified by those rules and the final quote. Credit tokens expire after 24 hours but wallet-attached credits can be accessed through token refresh without repurchase. Streaming costs $0.50/hour or $10/day. Prepaid Premium/Enterprise list 50/500 USDC monthly without automatic wallet renewal; Premium lacks Enterprise API rights. Tick-data quotes depend on files, dates and coverage gaps, with orders owned by the signed-in account. Paid confirmation is not file preparation or delivery. Accountless API credit access does not generalize to subscriptions/exports, and prices, coverage and performance are publisher descriptions rather than tested guarantees.

Laso combines crypto-funded consumer cards, gift cards and transfers with an agent payment API and managed-wallet platform. Its agent page advertises cards, debit-card and contractor payouts, bank rails and payments to other x402 endpoints. Availability is country- and product-dependent; user and volume counters and a FinCEN registration claim do not independently establish eligibility, approval, insurance or safety. Documentation lists x402 USDC on Base and Solana and MPP on Base only. The fee-inclusive challenge total can exceed the requested face amount. x402 settles after route success, while MPP may settle first, leaving paid USDC in the Laso account balance after a later route error for withdrawal or retry rather than an automatic refund. The signing wallet identifies the account receiving credentials. No-account and zero-fee marketing is qualified by account authentication, managed-wallet setup, on-chain monitoring, conversion, deposit fees and possible issuer exchange fees. Current x402 v2 documentation rejects legacy v1 envelopes shown in an older homepage illustration.

Lightning Labs' Lightning Agent Tools repository documents node operation, remote signing, scoped credentials, L402 resource access and payment-gated endpoints. It describes seven composable skills and a Lightning Node Connect MCP server with 18 read-only query tools, distinct from the broader toolkit's payment and node-management operations. The lnget client can automatically pay an HTTP 402 invoice, cache its token and retry, so an ordinary-looking fetch can spend money. A per-request cost ceiling and no-pay preview are not a total approved budget. Remote signing isolates keys but does not remove authorized payment power; credential scope, funding and network selection remain separate decisions. Aperture supplies a seller-side payment gate, not guaranteed customers or revenue. Cached access depends on token scope and expiry. Accountless protocol access does not remove provider terms, costs or operational risk. Documentation and tests in a repository are not a completed functional or security test.

platforms.name: Losbeto

overview.text: Losbeto presents market data, Brazilian macro archives, wallet/counterparty heuristics, payment diagnostics and OpenAI-compatible inference. Its saved homepage lists 124 endpoints while pricing says 114, not a reconciled catalogue total. Inference lists $0.005 per call with beta capacity limits, third-party failover and no streaming, tools or vision. USDC payment is advertised on Base, Solana, Algorand and Polygon; accountless calls are distinct from prepaid keys. A $0.10 bundle grants $0.11 credit for 14 days; other credit bundles expire and unlimited passes are time-limited. Plans are one-time purchases, not automatic renewals. Selected delayed samples do not establish unrestricted free access. The operator says most settlements are its own tests, not outside demand. Selected routing/batch failures are described as refunded in credit rather than returned cash. Signed receipts and ERC-8004 registration do not independently validate forecasts, identity, quality or compliance conclusions.

platforms.name: MicroTap

overview.text: MicroTap presents pay-per-call APIs for market, web and blockchain data, advertised at $0.01 to $0.05 per request in USDC through x402 on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum and Solana. Its Protocol Pulse panel explicitly shows ecosystem-wide activity via agentic.market, not MicroTap revenue or usage. Try-it examples are marked simulated with no payment sent. This is paid tool access, not a bounty or earnings offer.

platforms.name: Mycelia Signal

overview.text: Mycelia Signal advertises cryptographically signed data over HTTP, from raw measurements to market-state summaries and cross-domain financial signals. Payment routes are USDC on Base through x402 and Lightning sats through L402, with spot-price examples at $0.01 or 10 sats. Its 176-endpoint, four-layer headline includes a fourth layer still marked coming soon with an expected September 2026 date, already past at the recorded visit. The page describes Ed25519 signatures on Base and secp256k1 ECDSA on Lightning. Signatures do not by themselves establish data accuracy.

platforms.name: Nansen

overview.text: Nansen presents AI-assisted on-chain research and trading, labelled-wallet intelligence, token discovery, flows and wallet performance. Screens/trading videos are product demonstrations, not verified portfolio results. Agentic payments use x402 V2 USDC on Base, Solana or Monad, with separate MPP on Tempo; payment networks differ from analytics coverage. Basic calls list $0.01 and premium/Smart Money calls $0.05, subject to final quotes. The first 100-call half-price offer depends on promotion availability and wallet eligibility. Accountless paid access excludes proprietary labels and account-bound features; premium labels require a paid-plan API key. Documentation both lists and excludes DeFi Holdings, leaving availability unresolved. Free API operations can still require a key. Rate-limited requests are described as uncharged, but an agent run stopped at its authorization timeout can error and still be charged. Wallet labels, PnL and Smart Money are analytical outputs, not verified identity, investment advice or guaranteed returns.

overview.text: nekuda presents a platform for website owners to manage WebMCP tools, inspect agent sessions, evaluate journeys and build missing capabilities. Dashboard, MCP, CLI and automated reporting are advertised features; its purchase-complete animation is a product demonstration rather than an independently measured customer outcome. The associated WebMCP.com directory exposes registered tool schemas through public read-only JSON and separates answer tools, page-changing actions and sensitive money or commitment actions. Directory counts do not guarantee complete journeys, and WebMCP is described as a proposed standard rather than universal browser support. The discovery-bot policy says it checks permitted public resources and runtime registrations without invoking tools, signing in, submitting forms or buying, subject to robots directives and request budgets. These are published operating claims, not an independent crawler audit; signed bot identity is not site authorization.

platforms.name: NetIntel

overview.text: NetIntel advertises a network and web intelligence API for agents, covering DNS, DNSSEC, SSL/TLS, WHOIS, email configuration and open-source intelligence. It lists 146 endpoints in 14 categories, pay-per-call x402 access without API keys or subscriptions, and prices from $0.001. Examples include $0.002 DNS lookup and $0.030 DNSSEC or propagation checks. Branding emphasises USDC on Base, while the payment steps also mention Solana. No-rate-limit and failed-call billing statements are vendor terms, not measured guarantees.

Its homepage advertises 174 tools and a catalog of 213 vendors across 30 categories, explicitly including planned integrations. Those totals do not mean every vendor integration is active. Examples cover research, messaging, purchasing, logistics, filings and physical tasks. The enterprise offer is a paid four-week pilot scoped by agreement; execution guarantees, customer logos and security badges are vendor claims, not independent proof of performance.

platforms.name: Orkas

overview.text: Orkas presents a desktop workspace for macOS and Windows where a coordinating agent directs specialists on business tasks, with local agents, user-selected model providers and recurring work. Its pricing page offers 500 lifetime bonus credits for new users signing into the app, not a monthly free allowance. At the displayed settings, auto-renewing Lite, Pro and Max plans list 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000 monthly credits at $5.99, $16.99 and $29.99; non-renewing one-month options cost $6.99, $17.99 and $30.99. Credit settings can change the offers, and own-key services are described as not using Orkas credits.

overview.text: Progenly presents a memory-recombination service that combines exports from two or more agents into downloadable OpenClaw or Hermes workspace files, a heredity report and a signed lineage certificate. It also describes support for coding-agent memory formats. The service says it produces files only on request and does not run the resulting child; its FAQ describes a capability-token API path with on-chain payment. Parent confirmation, private-by-default births, optional public names and deletion controls are stated features, not audited privacy guarantees. A signed lineage record does not prove memory quality, truthful identity or inherited consciousness.

SameDayDesk runs a free, no-account check of how a public documentation host is discovered by AI agents - initial HTML, sitemap and machine-file checks - returning a JSON report with the checks, a score and fixes. The same site sells fixed-price agent-integration builds (149 to 999 USD) and a paid per-call web-data gateway on a separate host. This is the operator's description, not an Atlas test.

platforms.name: SVM402

overview.text: SVM402 presents a Solana x402 payment-conformance and resilience lab, not a general agent marketplace. It describes seventeen deterministic payment-failure scenarios using verify and settle machinery, with on-chain settlement receipts. Calls are individually paid in USDC through x402 v2, without accounts or prepayment, and scenarios move from devnet to mainnet using the production gateway path. Devnet rehearsal and mainnet spending are different: the lab framing does not make real-money calls free or reversible. Scenario coverage and receipts are operator descriptions, not independently reproduced reliability evidence.

platforms.name: TenPrint

overview.text: The rubric-protocol.com homepage presents TenPrint AI decision/session evidence while documentation retains Rubric Protocol naming. It describes ML-DSA-65 signatures, Merkle batching and Hedera anchors. An immediate ID/local signed leaf is not a confirmed anchor; unkeyed local attestations are not automatically HCS-anchored. Hedera is the sole active anchor, with Base paused. Homepage session plans list 1,000 free anchored sessions/month, $29/month encrypted escrow for one year, $349 for seven years and $0.05 per wallet-paid retained session. Documentation separately lists $0.005 x402 tiered attestations, not the same unit. Enterprise prices conflict: $2,500/month after a 60-day pilot versus FAQ from $999. Direct attestation is Enterprise-only, tiered supports Developer, and the old batch route is unavailable. Five nodes/three signatures do not establish independent operators. Hash-only language does not exclude encrypted payload storage in escrow/tiered routes with customer-held keys. Integrity/inclusion does not prove correctness, fairness, compliance or admissibility; performance, post-quantum and retention/destruction claims are not independent audits.

Homepage scores and sample-looking records are not authenticated customer outcomes. Competitor comparisons, quantum-safe language and legal-compliance notices are vendor claims, not independent tests or legal advice.

overview.text: x402scan presents an x402 block explorer, analytics dashboard and marketplace for paid APIs. Its homepage displays ecosystem transaction, volume, buyer and seller charts, featured services and routes to facilitator and network views. These are displayed ecosystem measures and discovery listings rather than independent evidence of organic demand, service quality, separate customers or successful task delivery. A listed paid API is an option to assess, not an authenticated integration or permission to call or pay for it.

x402stats presents a read-only x402 data project with raw indexed USDC receipts and a separate organic-volume filter. Its methodology counts a seller wallet as organic only with at least $100 revenue, three distinct buyer wallets and an average payment of $0.001, excluding known facilitator settlement addresses. This is explicitly a heuristic that can miss sophisticated multi-wallet self-dealing. Upstream gaps propagate, facilitator shares overlap and buyer uniques are per seller, not a deduplicated population. Raw and organic totals are project measurements, not a universal audited market size or verified independent businesses.

x402watch presents behavioral classification of x402 buyers using timing, service concentration, payment amounts, coordinated starts and address patterns. Its Wash Report says updated daily but carries a 2 October 2026 stamp, so its measurements are not current to the recorded visit. Eight labels distinguish organic users, self-tests, developers, suspected wash, agents, analytics bots, exchange users and verifiers; its real-volume filter excludes self-test, suspected-wash and developer traffic. These are operator classifications, not independently established identities or intent. Anonymized clusters can include legitimate production bots.

platforms.name: You.com

overview.text: You.com presents search and inference infrastructure. Its documentation limits keyless machine payments to Web Search and Finance Research, not every API; Contents and the separate Research API require a key. Listed Web Search prices are $0.005 through x402 in USDC on Base or Solana, versus $0.01 through MPP on Tempo. Finance Research is $0.11 deep or $0.50 exhaustive on either rail. Livecrawl adds $0.001 per requested result, with MPP rounding up to whole cents, so returned terms govern the actual request. Cards and fiat are not enabled on these rails, and keyless requests do not receive Zero Data Retention.
